description: Machine-readable relationship-type registry for the Jay Rosen Internet Archive knowledge graph. Formalizes allowed endpoint entity types, direction, inverse relationships, self-link and multi-assertion policy, temporal scope, and disputed-assertion support for every relationship type present in data/extracted_relationships.csv or in backend/entity_extraction_schema_v3.json. See data/README.md and scripts/validate-graph-data.mjs for how this is enforced, and issue #737 for the audit that produced it.

evidenceStandards.pipeline-default: Extracted from source record text by the entity-extraction pipeline (backend/entity_extraction_schema_v3.json), carrying a context snippet and a 0-1 confidence_score. The archive graph accepts assertions at any confidence today (no minimum threshold); acceptance is gated by referential integrity (extracted_entities.csv), the accepted/held relationship-type split (data/graph-validation-holds.json), and this registry's endpoint-type constraints.

migrationNotes.summary: Initial registry (issue #737). Endpoint-type constraints for accepted types are inferred from current usage in extracted_relationships.csv (falling back to backend/entity_extraction_schema_v3.json's valid_source_types/valid_target_types for the five types with zero current usage: Authored By, Quoted, Interviewed, Responds To, Founded). Legacy ambiguous types (Founded By, Owned By, Created, Covers) and the not-yet-wired Influenced type are marked status: "deferred" rather than guessed; their direction, inverse, symmetry, and temporal scope are curator decisions, not automation output.

Endpoint-type constraints for every accepted type now derive from backend/entity_extraction_schema_v3.json's valid_source_types/valid_target_types (curator-authored) instead of being inferred from current usage. That surfaced 3,390 existing relationship rows across 13 types whose recorded endpoint types the schema does not allow; each affected type now carries an endpointDivergence block (counts + example relationship IDs) and endpointEnforcement: "deferred" instead of silently widening the allowlist to match the dirty data. Types with no observed divergence carry endpointEnforcement: "enforced". Separately inventoried directionalContradictions on Originated By, Affiliated With, and Founded By record entity pairs where the same fact is asserted in both directions under one type. Owns gained a candidateInverseType (Owned By) so the duplicate-edge check can detect -- and, via data/graph-validation-holds.json duplicateEdgeExceptions, tolerate pending -- the small number of rows that already encode one ownership fact under both labels. None of this changes any type's status, direction, or temporal scope; it documents what the data already contains and defers cleanup to curator review, per issue #737's boundary.

temporalScope.note: "Affiliated With" is an ongoing state, not a single moment: Jay Rosen's affiliation with NYU can start and later end. extracted_relationships.csv has no start/end date column today, so this interval is not yet structurally captured; temporalScope: "interval" records that the gap is meaningful, for a future backfill to fill in.

temporalScope.assertion: Killing the Buddha: A Heretic’s Bible published in Free Press
temporalScope.note: "Published In" names a single publication event. It does not change or need a duration, so temporalScope: "instant" needs no additional date fields beyond the relationship's own extracted_date and the record it came from.

disputedAssertions.scenario: Two source records disagree on whether Organization X owns Organization Y (one reports a 2020 sale, the other still names the original owner).
disputedAssertions.note: extracted_relationships.csv has no negation, dispute, or superseded-by column, so this disagreement cannot be recorded as a qualified or disputed assertion today; both rows would sit in the graph as unqualified facts. disputedAssertionsAllowed is false for every type in this registry for that reason — it names a real gap in the row shape, not a per-type curator choice. Closing it needs a new column (or a status field) before any type's flag can turn true.

Quoted.description: Person or work A directly quotes person B.

Responds To.description: Person or work A is responding to or rebutting person, work, or event B.

Mentions.description: Entity A mentions entity B in passing or substantively.

Founded By.description: Legacy label used as an apparent inverse of Founded ("A Founded By B" intended to mean B founded A).
Founded By.deferralReason: Endpoint ordering is inconsistent across existing assertions: the source entity is sometimes the founder and sometimes the founded organization or work. Direction, formal inverse-of-Founded status, and symmetry cannot be inferred safely from current usage and are held pending curator review (see data/graph-validation-holds.json).

Owned By.description: Legacy label used as an apparent inverse of Owns ("A Owned By B" intended to mean B owns A).

Covers.description: Single legacy assertion of unclear scope, possibly press coverage of a person by an organization.

Influenced.description: Forward, outbound counterpart to Inspired By, Expands On, and Cites: source entity had a downstream effect the target can be traced to. Documented in data/SCHEMA.md as a count-0 forward declaration.
Influenced.deferralReason: Valid source and target types, and whether a record itself can be the influencer, are undecided. Not yet wired into the machine-enforced extraction schema (backend/entity_extraction_schema_v3.json) or the writer allowlists, so it stays unpopulated and unenforced until issues #344 and #548 resolve.
